acceptanceCriteria: A long-lived process that reads more distinct snapshot files than the cache holds keeps a bounded number of mappings, and deleted snapshot files release their blocks.
The V1-0947 guard test passes with -race, and every alias path (symbols, Source.Text, doccorpus) is either copied out or lease-scoped.
The index-snapshot spec records the lifetime contract; hot-path read cost is measured before and after.
body: Follow-up from the V1-0947 lane, 2026-10-07. Confirmed by measurement: with CORVINT_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT=pack or sectioned (opt-in; the default gob path does not map), evicted mappings are never unmapped; deleted snapshot files keep their disk blocks while mapped. Unmapping on ring eviction, and runtime.AddCleanup on the retained packFile, both SIGSEGV under the V1-0947 guard test (TestEvictedMappingsStayValidForEscapedAliases), because Symbol.Path, Symbol.Name, Source.Text() and doccorpus-retained Source values alias mapping bytes without keeping any owner alive. V1-0947 bounds mappings to distinct files by reusing the mapping of an unchanged file; this ticket covers releasing mappings at all. Design options: an explicit lifetime (lease or Close) with copy-out wherever an alias can outlive it, or heap-backed/copied bytes within the pack spec's 8 MB heap limit. Versions: corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 360); corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202; darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1.
